passage: The Petrov group investigated turnover of p53, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against p53; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of p53 was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of p53 remains 60 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 60 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Choosing 50% by stopping at the first half-life or 12.5% by overcounting; 60 min is two 30-minute half-lives, leaving 25%.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.B: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.C: It increases transcription of the gene
options.D: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide labels the protein or raises transcription; it blocks translation so the decay of the pre-existing pool can be followed.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of p53 remains after 150 minutes?
questions.trap: Choosing 96.875%, which is the percentage degraded rather than remaining; 150 min is five half-lives, leaving 3.125%.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining
options.B: The half-life is independent of starting concentration
options.C: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.D: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Believing a larger starting pool lengthens the half-life; for first-order decay t1/2 = ln 2/k is independent of starting amount.

questions.stem: p53 turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.B: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation
options.C: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.D: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Picking Golgi glycosylation, glycolytic-kinase phosphorylation or ribosome degradation because they sound regulatory; p53 is ubiquitinated and degraded by the proteasome.
